body:
AI transcription uses automatic speech recognition technologies to turn spoken words into written text and delivers transcripts with timestamps, speaker tags, and audio events.

Manually transcribing calls, videos, or meetings is laborious, especially when performed in real time. More organizations are turning to AI transcription tools to save time, improve productivity, and reduce costs.

This article explains how AI transcription works, key features to look for, benefits, and common use cases. It also expands into legal and compliance concerns when using AI transcription tools.

## Summary

• AI transcription uses speech to text models to convert audio recordings into textual format.

• When choosing an AI transcription tool, consider accuracy, speaker diarization, keyterm prompting, and other features your workflow needs.

• Organizations use AI transcription to improve transcribing productivity, analyze recordings at scale, streamline team collaboration, meet regulatory compliance, and more.

• Common use cases for AI transcription include meetings, content creation, and customer service, where teams often produce large volumes of audio recordings that need transcription.

• AI transcription is generally legal, but organizations must comply with privacy, consent, and local laws.

## What is AI transcription: How it works and what it captures

AI transcription converts spoken audio into written text using speech to text technologies. Modern AI transcription includes speaker tags, timestamps, and event tags to enrich the generated transcript. Organizations use AI transcription software to augment manual transcription or note-taking, allowing marketers, brand strategists, and content creators to focus on high-value tasks.

AI transcription relies on deep learning and natural language processing to produce accurate, contextually consistent, and structured transcripts. Some AI transcribers also use generative AI for post-processing, such as summarizing, searching, and extracting specific topics.

Generally, here’s how AI transcription works.

• Audio capture : The system records spoken conversations, whether in calls, meetings, or video, and sends them to a speech to text model. This can happen in real time or as post-recording audio files.

• Automatic speech recognition: The model analyzes the audio and predicts the words the speaker said, accounting for accents and context. Then, the model turns the audio into written text based on context it derives from the conversation stream.

• Formatting: The transcription model applies speaker tags and timestamps and differentiates pauses and background events, such as laughter, to enrich the transcript.

• Text delivery: Lastly, the AI transcription delivers the final transcript to you, which you can save or process further.

The final output of AI transcription is a textual record of narration, conversation, or speeches, structured with supporting data. You’ll know who spoke what, when each word was spoken through word-level timestamps, and punctuation that makes the transcript easier to read.

## Features to prioritize in AI transcription software

Organizations have unique transcription workflows that not all AI transcription tools can meet. Some might need a basic AI transcription tool, while others require advanced features that only select providers offer.

When choosing AI transcription software, consider the following:

• Accuracy : The transcription model should demonstrate high accuracy, regardless of use case. To know how accurate an AI transcription tool is, check its word error rate (WER). A lower rate means the tool is more accurate . WER also varies with audio quality and language, so test on your own recordings. For reference, ElevenLabs Scribe v3 makes 27% fewer word errors than Scribe v2 across 102 languages. ElevenLabs computes FLEURS WER per clip and then averages per language. Note that this methodology may produce different figures than alternative WER computation methods.

• Speaker diarization : A feature that allows the transcription system to identify different speakers in the audio and tag them accordingly in the transcript. Speaker diarization is useful for transcribing conversations involving multiple individuals.

• Multi-language support: The model transcribes audio in multiple languages . Some models also detect the spoken language automatically and handle switches between languages mid-conversation.

• Keyterm prompting: A vocabulary dictionary that helps the ASR model transcribe special phrases, such as brand names, correctly.

• Export and integrations: Beyond downloading transcripts directly to your computer, some AI transcription tools can send transcripts directly to CRMs and other enterprise applications.

• API support: Some AI transcription tools expose their transcription capabilities with an API. This allows engineering teams to embed transcription directly into existing products.

To learn more about choosing an AI transcription model , check out this guide .

Pro tip: Test AI transcription on real-world audio with background noise or overlapping conversations, not just clean samples. This gives you a more realistic expectation of how the tool will perform in real use.

## What are the benefits of AI transcription?

AI transcription offers multiple benefits to organizations, especially those that previously relied on manual transcription.

• Improve focus and productivity: During meetings or calls, participants can focus on the conversation instead of juggling note-taking.

• Save time and cost: Speech to text models can process large volumes of audio files quickly, letting human transcriptionists focus on high-stakes, complex tasks.

• Power data analytics: AI-generated transcripts, enriched with timestamps, audio tags, and speakers, support advanced data analytics. You can feed the transcript into an LLM-powered tool for summarization, entity extraction, or other analysis.
